data.one_liner: Provides a simple abstraction over Dart isolates for running code on background threads.
data.what_it_does: It offers a Worker class to manage a dedicated isolate with message passing, error/exit handling, and optional queue mode. It also includes a Parallel helper to run, map, or foreach functions across isolates.
use_when: You need to offload heavy CPU‑bound work without writing raw isolate boilerplate
You want a lightweight way to run functions in parallel on multiple isolates
avoid_when: You only need simple async futures (no separate thread needed)
You require platform‑specific native code or UI widgets
strengths: Minimal API for common isolate patterns
Supports queue mode and immediate disposal
weaknesses: Only supports primitive message types (objects must be plain data)
No built‑in support for stream‑based communication

alternatives.name: async
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides utilities like FutureGroup and StreamQueue for managing async tasks without isolates
